english.title: Smoking in a vehicle in which a child was present - England
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) smoked in

(A)_[a]_
(B)_[part, namely **(..SPECIFY PART OF VEHICLE..), of a]_

vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), that was smoke-free in that it was enclosed and more than one person was present in the vehicle, one of whom was a person under the age of 18
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 11(1A) of the Smoke-free (Exemptions and Vehicles) Regulations 2007 and section 7 of the Health Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
smoked
in a smoke-free vehicle

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 7(4) of the Act provides a defence where the person did not know, and could not reasonably have been expected to know, that it was a smoke-free place.
(ii) If it is the person in control or concerned in the management of the vehicle who is smoking, they would be liable for prosecution for this offence as well as failing to prevent smoking in a smoke-free vehicle (see CJS code HA06013 - PNLD document H12358), and may receive a fixed penalty fine for each offence
(iii) If the offence is committed in Wales see H12373 (CJS code HA06016)
